Since then she has continued to own it — reporting on legal's refund copy delay and resetting the launch to October 15 [[M2#1]][[M2#3]], booking Priya for the design review [[M2#28]][[M2#30]], and taking the action items from that review (updated mockups with the new fifteen percent discount and the middle-tier treatment by Thursday) [[M3#12]].

Northwind's invoices exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients — Marco got the email Sunday night [[M1#16]]. Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affects accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions, essentially just Northwind [[M1#17]]. Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected [[M1#19]].

The fix: Diego corrected the calculation that day and sent Northwind a note listing the affected invoice numbers by the next morning, while Marco called their CFO himself [[M1#20]][[M1#21]]. Marco told Diego not to promise any credit in the note until after the call [[M1#23]].

By the September 15 sync it was closed — corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco [[M2#9]]. Marco gave them one month free and asked Ana to apply the credit that day [[M2#10]][[M2#11]].

You chose **Drata** at the September 29 retro [[M1#19]].

**Why:** Marco presented three quotes — Vanta, Drata, and Secureframe — all within twenty percent of each other on price, so cost wasn't a differentiator; Drata had the best Postgres and GitHub integrations, which cover most of your evidence collection, while Vanta only offered a nicer dashboard and Secureframe was cheapest but had a smaller auditor network [[M1#16]]. Diego, who has to feed the platform, said integrations matter more than the dashboard, and Sofía backed Drata [[M1#17]][[M1#18]].

**Timeline attached to the decision:** Marco signs in the first week of October, and Diego starts the integrations after the checkout change ships — late October [[M1#19]][[M1#20]]. The audit itself is Q1, not this year, since evidence collection takes three months minimum; Marco said he'd give Northwind that timeline that week [[M1#22]]. Marco also noted SOC 2 is starting late because he sat on the quotes for a month, and said he won't own procurement going forward [[M1#23]].

Context: the vendor search was triggered by two customers asking for SOC 2 in August, one being Northwind, your biggest account [[M2#18]], with Ana originally naming Vanta and Drata as the obvious candidates [[M2#21]].

Fifteen percent. Marco announced on 22 September that finance wanted the annual discount cut from the twenty percent then shown on the page to fifteen, a change that came down on the Friday before [[M1#6]][[M1#8]]. He confirmed it as a decision he'd own: "the number is fifteen. That's a decision, I'll take the complaints." [[M1#11]]

On presentation, Priya argued the saving should appear in currency rather than only as a percentage — "Save 96 dollars a year" lands harder than "15 percent" [[M1#9]]. The agreed treatment is both: percent on the toggle, and the amount shown under each price [[M1#10]]. Ana said she would update the mockups with the new discount by Thursday [[M1#12]].

The biggest drop-off is at the **billing address step** in checkout.

- Initially Sofía only knew that roughly a third of people were lost between picking a plan and confirming payment, without knowing which step, because the funnel events weren't granular enough. [[M1#10]] Diego guessed the address form was the culprit, since the full billing address is requested even for card payments and Stripe doesn't need it. [[M1#11]]
- After Diego shipped the funnel events, the first data showed 28% of the people who pick a plan leave on the billing address screen. [[M2#10]][[M2#11]]
- With two more weeks of data, the figure firmed up at **29% dropping at the billing address step**, flat across plans and countries. [[M3#1]]

Sofía's recommendation on that basis: remove the address step for card payments (Stripe validates the postcode itself) and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans. [[M3#1]] Marco approved it — Diego and Ana build it, shipping one week after the pricing page, around 22 October. [[M3#6]][[M3#7]]
